```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Use quarto render to generate a static site in /docs
# Set github pages to deploy from main branch, /docs

# Insure packages are installed by checking required packages against installed packages
reqd_pkgs <- c("flextable",
               "sf",
               "tidyverse",
               "mapgl",
               "htmltools",
               "officer",
               "socratadata",
               "forcats")

install.packages(
  setdiff(
    reqd_pkgs,
    rownames(installed.packages())
  ),
  repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
)

lapply(reqd_pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE) |> 
  invisible()

# If needed, ensure that the Quarto render and RStudio read the same environment vars
readRenviron(".Renviron")

set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family  = "Authentic Sans",
  font.size    = 10,        # ~13px (flextable uses points)
  border.color = "#0b0b0b",
  background.color = "transparent",
  padding.top    = 8,
  padding.bottom = 4,
  padding.left   = 0,
  padding.right  = 16
)

# Wraps a data frame in a CIL-styled flextable ready to embed in the page.
# Columns size to their content by default. `widths` overrides that: one value
# per column, or named values setting just those columns. `max_width` caps the
# fitted widths, never the ones `widths` names. `full_height = TRUE` drops the
# 400px cap so the whole table renders inline without a vertical scrollbar.
# `unit = "%"` reads `widths` as shares of a full-width table instead of
# absolute sizes, which is how two tables are given matching columns.
# `fill` is a named vector of cell text -> background colour, letting a
# category be scanned down a column by colour as well as read.
# Usage: data |> cil_table(widths = c("Purpose of Funds" = 4))
#        data |> cil_table(widths = c(39, 61), unit = "%")
#        data |> cil_table(fill = c("Heavy Rain" = "#d1ddee"))
cil_table <- function(data, widths = NULL, heights = NULL,
                      max_width = NULL, unit = "in", full_width = TRUE,
                      full_height = FALSE, fill = NULL) {
  ft <- flextable(data)
  pct <- identical(unit, "%")
  # Percentages never reach flextable, so they don't take the fitted path below.
  fitted <- !pct && !(is.null(widths) && is.null(max_width))

  if (pct) {
    if (is.null(widths)) {
      stop("`unit = \"%\"` sets column shares, so it needs `widths`.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(max_width)) {
      stop("`max_width` caps fitted widths in absolute units; `unit = \"%\"` ",
           "sets shares outright. Use one or the other.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!full_width) {
      stop("Percentage widths are shares of a full-width table. Leave ",
           "`full_width = TRUE`.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(heights)) {
      # `unit` covers heights too, and a row can't be a percentage of anything.
      stop("`heights` needs an absolute unit, which `unit = \"%\"` overrides. ",
           "Set column shares and row heights in separate calls.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (length(widths) != ncol(data)) {
      # Named subsets work for absolute widths because dim_pretty() supplies a
      # baseline for the columns left out. Shares have no such baseline.
      stop("`widths` has ", length(widths), " value(s) but `data` has ",
           ncol(data), " column(s). Percentage widths need one per column.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }

  if (fitted && full_width) {
    stop("`full_width` stretches columns to the container; `widths`/`max_width` ",
         "pin them. Use one or the other.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!fitted) {
    # Browser-side content fitting, like Excel's Autofit. width = 0 leaves the
    # table unconstrained; width = 1 would stretch it to 100% regardless of text.
    ft <- set_table_properties(ft, if (full_width) 1 else 0, layout = "autofit")
  } else {
    # Fitted widths are the baseline, capped by max_width, then overridden by
    # anything `widths` names. "autofit" discards widths, so this must be fixed.
    fit <- unlist(dim_pretty(ft)$widths)
    if (!is.null(max_width)) fit <- pmin(fit, max_width)
    if (is.null(widths)) {
      widths <- fit
    } else if (!is.null(names(widths)) && all(nzchar(names(widths)))) {
      unknown <- setdiff(names(widths), names(data))
      if (length(unknown)) {
        stop("`widths` names no such column: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "),
             call. = FALSE)
      }
      fit[match(names(widths), names(data))] <- widths
      widths <- fit
    } else if (length(widths) != ncol(data)) {
      # Otherwise they land on the first columns, misaligning every one.
      stop("`widths` has ", length(widths), " value(s) but `data` has ",
           ncol(data), " column(s). Give one width per column, or name them.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    ft <- set_table_properties(ft, layout = "fixed")
    ft <- width(ft, j = seq_along(widths), width = widths, unit = unit)
  }

  if (!is.null(heights)) {
    # Heights are only emitted under the "exact" rule; "auto" ignores them.
    ft <- height(ft, height = heights, part = "body", unit = unit)
    ft <- hrule(ft, rule = "exact", part = "body")
  }

  if (!is.null(fill)) {
    unknown <- setdiff(names(fill), unlist(lapply(data, as.character)))
    if (length(unknown)) {
      stop("`fill` names a value no cell holds: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "),
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    # bg() hands the function one column at a time, so the lookup is on the cell
    # text itself. Anything unnamed -- ids, counts -- keeps the table's own
    # background rather than picking up a colour by accident.
    ft <- bg(ft, part = "body", bg = function(x) {
      matched <- fill[as.character(x)]
      ifelse(is.na(matched), "transparent", matched)
    })
  }

  # flextable's width() speaks only in/cm/mm, and autofit emits no column widths
  # at all, so shares are carried by markup instead: a <colgroup> the browser
  # obeys once .scroll-output--pct switches the table to `table-layout: fixed`.
  # Empty otherwise, leaving the sub() below a no-op.
  colgroup <- if (pct) {
    paste0("<colgroup>",
           paste0(sprintf('<col style="width:%s%%;">', widths), collapse = ""),
           "</colgroup>")
  } else ""

  ft |>
    border_remove() |>
    bold(bold = TRUE, part = "header") |>
    hline(border = fp_border(color = "#0b0b0b", width = 1.5),  part = "header") |>
    hline(border = fp_border(color = "#969696", width = 0.75), part = "body") |>
    # hline() mirrors each rule onto the next row's top edge as well as the
    # current row's bottom. Under the `border-collapse: separate` these tables
    # need for sticky headers, the two edges stack instead of merging, so every
    # interior rule renders at double weight -- only the final one, with no row
    # below it, looks right. Clearing the tops leaves a single 0.75pt line.
    border(border.top = fp_border(width = 0), part = "body") |>
    padding(
      padding.top = 0, padding.bottom = 4,
      padding.left = 0, padding.right = 8,
      part = "header"
    ) |>
    padding(
      padding.left = 2, padding.right = 8,
      part = "body"
    ) |> 
    # Both steps are needed to keep the table out of a shadow DOM, which no page
    # CSS can reach: ft.shadow drops the static host, and the rename hides the
    # wrapper from tabwid.js, which shadow-roots every .tabwid on DOMContentLoaded.
    htmltools_value(ft.shadow = FALSE) |>
    as.character() |>
    sub(pattern = 'class="tabwid"', replacement = 'class="cil-tabwid"', fixed = TRUE) |>
    sub(pattern = "(<table[^>]*>)", replacement = paste0("\\1", colgroup)) |>
    HTML() |>
    div(class = paste(
      c("scroll-output",
        if (fitted) "scroll-output--fit",
        if (pct) "scroll-output--pct",
        if (full_height) "scroll-output--full"),
      collapse = " "
    ))
}

```
# Hazard Categories

The Queens Resource Map will display ranked hazard-related preparedness and recovery resources and messaging at the Community District Tabulation Area (CDTA) level. 

Our hazard categorization is based on New York City's 2024 Jurisdictional Risk Assessment[^1] report. The 2024 report uses the Pennsylvania Public Health Risk Assessment Tool (PHRAT) model in order to develop a "Planning Priority Score" used to suggest where New York City should focus its resources and planning efforts. The ten categories defined by the 2024 JRA report and their rank are: 

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~Rank, ~`JRA Hazard`,
    "1", "Flooding",
    "2", "Hazardous Materials Release",
    "3", "Pandemic",
    "4", "Infectious Disease Outbreak",
    "5", "Coastal Storm",
    "6", "Mass Casualty Event",
    "7", "Chemical Threats",
    "8", "Temperature Extremes",
    "9", "Utility Interruption",
    "10", "Cyberattack"
  ),
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%",
  full_height = TRUE
)
```

Our intended user is a New Yorker concerned about an imminent threat, rather than a municpal agency or staffer. To support this use case, we've modified the hazard categorization accordingly:

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~`Queens Map Hazard`, ~Notes,
    "Heavy Rain", "Added to capture non-coastal stormwater flooding",
    "Coastal Storm", "",
    "Extreme Heat", "Broken out from Temperature Extremes",
    "Extreme Cold", "Broken out from Temperature Extremes",
    "Hazmat / Chemical", "Combines Hazardous Materials Release and Chemical Threats",
    "Mass Casualty Event / Active Shooter", "Extends Mass Casualty Event",
    "Infectious Disease", "Combines Pandemic and Infectious Disease Outbreak",
    "Blackout & Cyberattack (EMP)", "Combines Utility Interruption and Cyberattack"
  ),
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%"
)
```
[^1]: [Jurisdictional Risk Assessment 2024, New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/498014fede58495dae447d97c6bf1611)

# Exploratory Analysis

## Data Sources
Hazard ranking among Queens CDTAs requires data sources that can be used to differentiate the relative risks between districts. These data are not available for all hazards:

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~`Queens Map Hazard`, ~`Data Source`,
    "Heavy Rain", "Stormwater Flood Maps",
    "Coastal Storm", "Current-day Storm Surge FVI",
    "Extreme Heat", "Heat Vulnerability Index",
    "Extreme Cold", "None available",
    "Hazmat / Chemical", "Chemically Intensive Small Businesses\nHazardous Waste Material Storage",
    "Mass Casualty Event / Active Shooter", "None available",
    "Infectious Disease", "Pandemic Influenza Vulnerability Index",
    "Blackout & Cyberattack (EMP)", "None available"
  ),
  full_height = TRUE,
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%"
)
```

In the absence of available information at the Community District level, extreme cold, mass casualty events / active shooter incidents, and blackout & cyberattack cannot be ranked.

In order to identify a suitable ranking methodology for the remaining hazards, a discussion of the disparate data is warranted. 

```{r}
#| cache: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Fetch data sources

cdta <- read_sf("https://services5.arcgis.com/GfwWNkhOj9bNBqoJ/arcgis/rest/services/NYC_Community_District_Tabulation_Areas_2020/FeatureServer/0/query?where=CDTAType=0&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson") |> 
  mutate(cdtaCode = paste0(
    BoroCode,
    str_sub(CDTA2020, -2)
  ))

stormwater_limited <- read_sf("https://github.com/BetaNYC/q-map/releases/download/data-v4/stormwater_limited_1_77.geojson") |> st_make_valid()

stormwater_moderate <- read_sf("https://github.com/BetaNYC/q-map/releases/download/data-v4/stormwater_moderate_2_13.geojson") |> 
  st_make_valid()

ss_cur_fvi <- soc_read(
  "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Environment/New-York-City-s-Flood-Vulnerability-Index/mrjc-v9pm.json",
  query = soc_query(
    select = "the_geom, GEOID, ss_cur"
  ),
  include_synthetic_cols = FALSE
)

hvi <- read_sf("https://services1.arcgis.com/8cuieNI8NbqQZQVJ/arcgis/rest/services/HVI_by_CDTA_CRAD_2024/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

chem_small_biz <- read_sf("https://services3.arcgis.com/A6Zjpzrub8ESZ3c7/arcgis/rest/services/Chemically%20Intensive%20Small%20Businesses_2/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

hazmat_storage <- read_sf("https://services6.arcgis.com/yG5s3afENB5iO9fj/arcgis/rest/services/EPA_RCA_Fuel_Oil_Storage/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

pivi <- read_sf("https://services1.arcgis.com/8cuieNI8NbqQZQVJ/arcgis/rest/services/Pandemic_Influenza_Vulnerability_Index/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

# Aggregate where needed

## Stormwater -> CDTA
stormwater_all <- st_union(
  st_union(stormwater_limited),
  st_union(stormwater_moderate)
) |> 
  st_transform(4326) |> 
  st_make_valid()

stormwater_pct <- cdta |> 
  mutate(cdta_area = st_area(geometry)) |> 
  st_intersection(stormwater_all) |> 
  transmute(CDTA2020,
            stormwater_pct = as.numeric(st_area(geometry) / cdta_area) * 100) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(stormwater_pct) |> 
  mutate(stormwater_pct = replace_na(stormwater_pct, 0))

## Tract-level FVI -> CDTA
# Assign max FVI to CD
ss_cur_fvi_cd <- ss_cur_fvi |> 
  st_join(cdta |> select(CDTA2020),
          largest = TRUE)

ss_cur_fvi_cd <- ss_cur_fvi_cd |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(CDTA2020) |> 
  summarize(max_ss_cur_fvi = max(ss_cur, na.rm = T))
 
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(ss_cur_fvi_cd)

# Hazmat storage
cdta$hazmat_count <- lengths(st_intersects(cdta, hazmat_storage))

# Join remainder

## HVI
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(hvi |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(CommDist, HVI),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == CommDist))

## Chemically Intensive Small Business count
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(chem_small_biz |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(BoroCD, top_3) |> 
              mutate(BoroCD = as.character(BoroCD)) |> 
              rename(chem_count = "top_3"),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == BoroCD))

## PIVI
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(pivi |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(COMMDIST, PIVI),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == COMMDIST))

cdta <- cdta |> 
  select(BoroCode,CDTA2020, cdtaCode, CDTAName,
         stormwater_pct, max_ss_cur_fvi, hazmat_count, HVI, chem_count, PIVI) |> 
  relocate(geometry, .after = last_col()) |> 
  mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = as.integer(max_ss_cur_fvi))
```

## Heavy Rain

The impact of heavy rain on a given Community District is taken as the percent area that experiences stormwater flooding of any kind (i.e. greater than 4 inches of flooding without sea level rise under a limited- or moderate-intensity rainfall event)[^2]. Citywide, this percentage ranges from `r round(min(cdta$stormwater_pct),2)`% to `r round(max(cdta$stormwater_pct),2)`%. In Queens, the percentage ranges from `r round(min(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$stormwater_pct),2)`% to `r round(max(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$stormwater_pct),2)`%. All 59 Community Districts experience some stormwater flooding.

```{r}
boro_fill <- list(
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = NULL,
    values = c(`TRUE` = "#3258a3", `FALSE` = "#cedef0"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "Queens", `FALSE` = "Other Boroughs"),
    breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE)
  ),
  theme(
    legend.position      = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.margin        = margin(t = 0, b = 6),
    legend.key.size      = unit(11, "pt"),
    legend.text          = element_text(size = 9)
  )
)

ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, stormwater_pct), 
               y = stormwater_pct,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Stormwater Flood Extent in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Stormwater Flood Extent [%]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill
```

[^2]: [NYC Stormwater Flood Maps](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Environment/NYC-Stormwater-Flood-Maps/9i7c-xyvv/about_data)

## Coastal Storm

The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene's Flood Vulnerability Index estimates neighborhood vulnerability to flooding by combining susceptibility to harm and capacity to recover[^3]. This project makes use of the storm surge index based on current-current day sea level. 
CDTAs are assigned an FVI value of 1-5 based on the maximum census tract value that overlaps with the district boundary. Based on this approach, `r sum(!is.na(cdta$max_ss_cur_fvi))` of 59 NYC CDTAs are vulnerable to coastal flooding; `r sum(!is.na(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$max_ss_cur_fvi))` of `r cdta |> filter(BoroCode == 4) |> nrow()` Queens CDTAs are vulnerable to coastal flooding:

```{r}
cil_table(cdta |> 
            st_drop_geometry() |> 
            filter(BoroCode == 4) |> 
            select(CDTAName, max_ss_cur_fvi) |> 
            mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = as.character(max_ss_cur_fvi)) |> 
            rename(
              "CDTA Name" = "CDTAName",
              "Storm Surge FVI, 2020s" = "max_ss_cur_fvi"
            ),
          full_height = TRUE
          )
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, max_ss_cur_fvi, .na_rm = F, .default = -Inf), 
               y = max_ss_cur_fvi,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$max_ss_cur_fvi, na.rm = T),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Flood Vulnerability Index in CDTAs",
       subtitle = "Storm Surge, 2020s Sea Level",
       x = "CDTA", y = "FVI [1-5]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$max_ss_cur_fvi, na.rm = T),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill
```


[^3]: [Flood Vulnerability Index](https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/flood-vulnerability-index/)

## Extreme Heat

Similarly, DOHMH's Heat Vulnerability Index combines neighborhood environmental and social factors to detail the distribution of the risk of death from heat[^4]. Unlike the FVI, the HVI is released at the CDTA level, so aggregation is not necessary. 

[^4]: [Heat Vulnerability Index](https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/hvi/)
```{r}
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, HVI), 
               y = HVI,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$HVI),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Heat Vulnerability Index in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "HVI [1-5]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$HVI),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill
```


## Hazmat / Chemical

Two hazmat / chemical threat data sources are referenced in the 2024 JRA report. 

The first is a dataset of Chemically Intensive Small Businesses, which provides a count of these businesses per CDTA[^5]. The count ranges from `r min(cdta$chem_count)` to `r max(cdta$chem_count)` citywide; In Queens, the range is from `r min(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$chem_count)` to `r max(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$chem_count)`. Notably, `r cdta |> filter(BoroCode == 4 & chem_count > median(cdta$chem_count)) |> nrow()` of `r cdta |> filter(BoroCode == 4) |> nrow()` Queens CDTAs have more chemically intensive small businesses than the citywide median. The CDTA with the highest number of chemically intensive small businesses is `r cdta |> arrange(desc(chem_count)) |> slice(1) |> pull(CDTAName) |> str_split_i(" ", 2)`.

```{r}
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, chem_count), 
               y = chem_count,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$chem_count),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Chemically Intensive Small Businesses in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Count") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$chem_count),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill

```

The second dataset contains the locations of Fuel Oil / Hazardous Waste Material Storage sites across the city[^6]. These data come from the  EPA's Resource Conservation and Recovery Act biennial report. There are `r nrow(hazmat_storage)` sites citywide.Counting sites per district gives a range of `r min(cdta$hazmat_count)` to `r max(cdta$hazmat_count)`; in Queens the range is `r min(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$hazmat_count)` to `r max(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$hazmat_count)`. Sites are mapped below:

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Compute quintiles for choropleth map
hazmat_breaks <- quantile(cdta$hazmat_count, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), type = 1)
hazmat_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("grey80", "#efd1cc", "#db7a6b", "#a44132"))(5)

# Bin labels based on breaks
bin_low  <- c(min(cdta$hazmat_count), unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]))
bin_high <- c(unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]) - 1, max(cdta$hazmat_count))
bin_labels <- ifelse(bin_low == bin_high, bin_low, paste0(bin_low, "–", bin_high))

# HTML popups
hazmat_sites <- hazmat_storage |>
  mutate(hazmat_popup = paste0("<strong>", HANDLER_NA, "</strong><br/>", TOP3))

maplibre(bounds = cdta,
         style = carto_style("positron")) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "hazmat-count",
    source = cdta,
    fill_color = step_expr(
      column = "hazmat_count",
      base   = hazmat_colors[1],
      values = unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]),
      stops  = hazmat_colors[-1]
    ),
    fill_opacity = 0.85,
    fill_outline_color = "#ffffff",
    popup = "CDTAName"
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id = "hazmat-sites",
    source = hazmat_sites,
    circle_color = "#0b0b0b",
    circle_radius = 4,
    circle_stroke_color = "#ffffff",
    circle_stroke_width = 1,
    popup = "hazmat_popup"
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Hazmat sites per CDTA",
    values = bin_labels,
    colors = hazmat_colors,
    type = "categorical",
    style = list(
      background_color = "#fefcfa",
      backgroud_opacity = 0.8
    )
  )
```

# Hazard Ranking

As three of the five rankable hazards (coastal storm, extreme heat, infectious disease) are described using a 1 -5 vulnerability index, an initial approach to ranking the disparate hazards is to express the other two  (heavy rain, hazmat/chemical) in terms of quintiles denoted 1 -5. As a simplification, the count of hazmat and fuel oil storage sites per CDTA may be added to the count of chemically intensive small businesses per CDTA. For the purposes of district-level hazard ranking, districts not exposed to coastal storm surge are assigned an FVI value of 0 rather than `NA`.

```{r}
# Create quintile columns
cdta <- cdta |> 
  # Add hazmat and chemically intensive small businesses first
  mutate(hazmat_chem_count = hazmat_count + chem_count) |>
  mutate(
    sw_quintile = cut(
      stormwater_pct,
      breaks = quantile(stormwater_pct, probs = seq(0,1,0.2)),
      labels = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE
    ),
    hazmat_quintile = cut(
      hazmat_chem_count,
      breaks = quantile(hazmat_chem_count, probs = seq(0,1,0.2)),
      labels = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  )
```

The resulting quintile ranks for stormwater flooding:
```{r}
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, sw_quintile), 
               y = sw_quintile,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$sw_quintile),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(

    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),

    )+
  labs(title = "Stormwater Flooding Quintile Rank in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Count") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$sw_quintile),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill
```

```{r}
hazard_names <- c(
  sw_quintile     = "Heavy Rain",
  max_ss_cur_fvi  = "Coastal Storm",
  HVI             = "Extreme Heat",
  hazmat_quintile = "Hazmat / Chemical",
  PIVI            = "Infectious Disease"
)



ranked <- cdta |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(BoroCode == 4) |> 
  mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = replace_na(max_ss_cur_fvi, 0)) |> 
  select(CDTA2020, max_ss_cur_fvi, HVI, PIVI, sw_quintile, hazmat_quintile) |> 
  pivot_longer(-CDTA2020, names_to = "hazard", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(hazard = recode(hazard, !!!hazard_names)) |>
  arrange(CDTA2020, desc(score), hazard) |>
  mutate(rank  = paste("Rank", row_number()),
         label = paste0(hazard, " (", score, ")"), .by = CDTA2020) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = CDTA2020, names_from = rank, values_from = label) |> 
  rename(CDTA = CDTA2020)

# One tint per hazard, all at ~88% lightness so no category outweighs another.
# Heavy Rain and Hazmat carry the blue and red already used by the choropleths.
hazard_fill <- c(
  "Heavy Rain"         = "#d1ddee",
  "Hazmat / Chemical"  = "#efd1cc",
  "Extreme Heat"       = "#f3f0ce",
  "Infectious Disease" = "#cef3da",
  "Coastal Storm"      = "#eecef3"
)

# Cells read "Heavy Rain (5)", so the tints are re-keyed onto the labels the
# table actually holds -- built from the data so a new score can't miss a colour.
rank_labels <- unique(unlist(ranked[-1]))
label_fill <- setNames(
  unname(hazard_fill[sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", rank_labels)]),
  rank_labels
)

cil_table(ranked,
          full_height = TRUE,
          fill = label_fill
          )


```

Considerations based on this initial ranking:

1. **Queens has many chemically intensive small businesses compared to other boroughs.** This comes across in the rankings, where 11 of 14 Queens districts have Hazmat/Chemical ranked in position 1 or 2.
2. **Queens is less vulnerable to infectious disease than other boroughs**. The only districts that do not have infectious disease ranked last are those Queens districts which are not exposed to coastal storm surge. All Queens districts have a PIVI score of 1 or 2. 

We may then, ask what the ranking looks among only heavy rain, coastal storm, and extreme heat:

```{r}
hazard_names_3 <- c(
  sw_quintile     = "Heavy Rain",
  max_ss_cur_fvi  = "Coastal Storm",
  HVI             = "Extreme Heat"
)

ranked_3 <- cdta |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(BoroCode == 4) |> 
  mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = replace_na(max_ss_cur_fvi, 0)) |> 
  select(CDTA2020, max_ss_cur_fvi, HVI, sw_quintile) |> 
  pivot_longer(-CDTA2020, names_to = "hazard", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(hazard = recode(hazard, !!!hazard_names_3)) |>
  arrange(CDTA2020, desc(score), hazard) |>
  mutate(rank  = paste("Rank", row_number()),
         label = paste0(hazard, " (", score, ")"), .by = CDTA2020) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = CDTA2020, names_from = rank, values_from = label) |> 
  rename(CDTA = CDTA2020)

hazard_fill_3 <- c(
  "Heavy Rain"         = "#d1ddee",
  "Extreme Heat"       = "#f3f0ce",
  "Coastal Storm"      = "#eecef3"
)

rank_labels_3 <- unique(unlist(ranked_3[-1]))
label_fill_3 <- setNames(
  unname(hazard_fill[sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", rank_labels_3)]),
  rank_labels_3
)

cil_table(ranked_3,
          full_height = TRUE,
          fill = label_fill_3
          )
```

This second ranking highlights the need for hazard prioritization in the case of tied scores between hazards. One approach would be to consider geographic specificity. Coastal storm threat would come first, as it is the only hazard that is not city-wide. Next comes heavy rain, which is a citywide concern, but only of concern in specific areas that experience stormwater flooding. Last, then, would be extreme heat, whose spatial distribution is heterogeneous, but less acutely so than the other two threats, at least in terms of the physical environment. 

```{r}
hazard_names_3 <- c(
  sw_quintile     = "Heavy Rain",
  max_ss_cur_fvi  = "Coastal Storm",
  HVI             = "Extreme Heat"
)

hazard_priority_3 <- c("Coastal Storm", "Heavy Rain", "Extr
eme Heat")

ranked_3 <- cdta |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(BoroCode == 4) |> 
  mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = replace_na(max_ss_cur_fvi, 0)) |> 
  select(CDTA2020, max_ss_cur_fvi, HVI, sw_quintile) |> 
  pivot_longer(-CDTA2020, names_to = "hazard", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(hazard = recode(hazard, !!!hazard_names_3)) |>
  arrange(CDTA2020, desc(score), match(hazard, hazard_priority_3)) |>
  mutate(rank  = paste("Rank", row_number()),
         label = paste0(hazard, " (", score, ")"), .by = CDTA2020) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = CDTA2020, names_from = rank, values_from = label) |> 
  rename(CDTA = CDTA2020)

hazard_fill_3 <- c(
  "Heavy Rain"         = "#d1ddee",
  "Extreme Heat"       = "#f3f0ce",
  "Coastal Storm"      = "#eecef3"
)

rank_labels_3 <- unique(unlist(ranked_3[-1]))
label_fill_3 <- setNames(
  unname(hazard_fill[sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", rank_labels_3)]),
  rank_labels_3
)

cil_table(ranked_3,
          full_height = TRUE,
          fill = label_fill_3
          )
```

The remaining hazard categories would then be pinned based on subject matter expert feedback, e.g.:

1. Ranked
2. Ranked
3. Ranked 
4. **Hazmat / Chemical**
5. **Infectious Disease**
6. **Extreme Cold**
7. **Mass Casualty / Active Shooter Event**
8. **Blackout / Cyberattack (EMP)**
